title: Try to allow `f16` vectors in storage
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently qdrant uses hard-coded f32 as a data type for all vectors (except quantized).
But in many applications storing f32 might be too expensive and redundant. 

It would be interesting to try to eventually migrate to dynamic switch between f16 and f32 precisions.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

As a first step of the migration, we'd like to experiment with compile-time switch first.

To do this, we would need to introduce a feature-flag, that would switch from f32 to f16.

Make sure that all qdrant functions work properly with f16 type enabled, such as:

- quantization
- mmaps
- querying
- indexing
- ...

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Make storage type generic, but this easily might be too much effort for a single PR, so it is better to postpone for another iteration.

**Additional context**

We would need to pay extra attention for query types, as interface (REST and gRPC) should not change once we switch to f16.


---

Note for contributors: Please consider this as tracking issue. If you think that it would be beneficial to split the task into multiple smaller PRs, please you are welcome to do so. Bounty will be rewarded for each PR independently

/attempt #3333 Previous PR #4032. Based on feedback, reduce the scope of the changes to just vector_storage, not change data_types::vectors::VectorElementType. All changes within segment crate. f16 feature (adds half dependency). Implement data_types::primitive::PrimitiveVectorElement for f16. In vector_storage::vector_storage_base: ``` #[cfg(not(feature = "f16"))] pub(crate) type VectorStorageElementType = VectorElementType; #[cfg(feature = "f16")] pub(crate) type VectorStorageElementType = half::f16; ``` This will be the type used in VectorStorageEnum: ``` pub enum VectorStorageEnum { DenseSimple(SimpleDenseVectorStorage), DenseMemmap(Box>), DenseAppendableMemmap(Box>), SparseSimple(SimpleSparseVectorStorage), MultiDenseSimple(SimpleMultiDenseVectorStorage), } ``` Add new mod spaces::metric_f16 (feature f16). Implement spaces::Metric for all metrics. For types::Distance, make vector functions generic: ``` impl Distance { pub fn preprocess_vector( &self, vector: DenseVector, ) -> TypedDenseVector where CosineMetric: Metric, EuclidMetric: Metric, DotProductMetric: Metric, ManhattanMetric: Metric; pub fn similarity(&self, v1: &[T], v2: &[T]) -> ScoreType where CosineMetric: Metric, EuclidMetric: Metric, DotProductMetric: Metric, ManhattanMetric: Metric; } ``` These are called with both VectorElementType and VectorStorageElementType. Implementers of vector_storage::query_scorer::QueryScorer and related functions would be generic over `TMetric: Metric` (and VectorElementType as required). For example (vector_storage::raw_scorer): ``` fn new_multi_scorer_with_metric< 'a, TMetric: Metric + Metric + 'a, TVectorStorage: MultiVectorStorage, >( query: QueryVector, vector_storage: &'a TVectorStorage, point_deleted: &'a BitSlice, is_stopped: &'a AtomicBool, ) -> OperationResult>; ``` This is because the query is VectorElementType, while vector_storage is VectorStorageElementType.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I've rebased my changes after the generic storage landed in #3900.

I apologize for a half-baked pull-request, but I otherwise would feel guilty to comment on the issue without having submitted anything.

I'm very excited about f16, and I'd love to contribute this very feature to Qdrant to see what speedups it could bring.
However, I believe it may not be practical to proceed with this contribution right now, because there are following prerequisites not met:
* `quantization`, which lives in a separate repository, does not have the corresponding `f16` switch, and I don't see a linked issue in the description;
* even if we adapt `quantization` to handle `f16`, we are left with reimplementing distances with f16 SIMDs, and this is a real obstacle, see below;
* the holy grail of this issue, so far as i understood it, is to calculate the distance without having to cast between floats of different widths, but until the language supports `f16` natively, we are still left with some casts here and there, and this still worsens the developer experience.

## f16 SIMD
As mentioned above, the native support of f16 in the language would allow us to write `(-1..=+1)` without having to do the squats with num-traits along the lines of `let one = VectorElementType::ONE; (-one..=one)` and suchlike.

Even if the language supports natively f16 one day, we'll have to expand our SIMD implementations accordingly, and, at least for NEON, the f16-wide intrinsics are not passed through to the stdlib. That is, without resorting to hand-written assembly, you can have `vfmaq_f32`, but not `vfmaq_f16`.

There is even an issue for that, but that one is apparently stall:
https://github.com/rust-lang/stdarch/issues/344

## GPGPU
In theory, if we absolutely need f16 in Qdrant, I could do that through GPU, because almost all server-grade GPUs support fp16 now. But that would require a massive overhaul across the whole Qdrant, so this is far outside the scope of this issue.

----

All in all, I believe this issue is best postponed until one of the above happens. At the very least, I believe we should rip "good first issue" tag off it: it may be deceptively simple, but, in my experience, at the current state of affairs, it is not beginner-friendly at all, and it attracts contributors who end up in a dead end.

@reporter, @participant10, would love you to chime in!
